headlines.article_text: Walmart (WMT) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Walmart narrowly topped fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates. The retailer also raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook. The company highlighted e-commerce sales growth as it said it saw success with store-fulfilled pickup and delivery. In this article WMT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers enter a Walmart store in Charlotte, North Carolina, Aug. 30, 2026. Travis Dove | Bloomberg | Getty Images Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season. "This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," CFO John David Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses." Walmart said global e-commerce sales grew 17%, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter. Rainey said that growth was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and lowered prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter. Walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices. With the growth, Walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to rise between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared to previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey said Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance. Walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth. "We feel like, in the face of what has been kind of a volatile couple years between tariffs and high diesel prices, we've navigated this really well, which I think really underscores the durability of our earning streams," Rainey said. Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 65 cents adjusted vs. 64 cents expected Revenue: $188.84 billion vs. $187.27 billion expected For the quarter ended Oct. 31, the company reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, the year prior. Revenue rose 5.2%. Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from the year prior. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount. Sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise. The company is typically well-insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter , the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef. Rainey said on Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start." The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership. In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships, as well. Though the company reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey said it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more." The company on Thursday said its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter. Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date. headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO live updates: ANT stock price and Nasdaq debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 2:18 02:18 Anthropic's IPO could mint thousands of millionaires — and reshape San Francisco Tech Anthropic is set for its long-awaited Nasdaq debut on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab raised over $81 billion in a record IPO , surpassing SpaceX 's offering in June. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. Its fully diluted market cap sits at around $1.5 trillion. Tune in at 10:00 a.m. ET as Dario and Daniela Amodei join CNBC TV exclusively to talk about the debut. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT," and its debut will be a big test for the AI industry. Investors have been fretting over Jensen Huang's sudden ouster at Nvidia , voters' stinging rebuke of AI during the midterm elections and the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout . "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort." Read more CNBC news on Anthropic Anthropic IPO live updates: ANT stock price and Nasdaq debut Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX How to get Anthropic stock — without buying the IPO Small investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut Meet the seven co-founders of Anthropic Anthropic's Wall Street whisperer: CFO Krishna Rao CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. 23 Min Ago Academics and industry experts circulate ‘The MisAnthropic Statement’ ahead of listing More than 90 academics and AI safety experts signed " The MisAnthropic Statement " ahead of the company's Nasdaq debut, blasting it for amassing power and rushing to build potentially dangerous technology. "Anthropic warns that recursively self-improving AI could concentrate power and escape human control, yet races to build it first," the statement says. "The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation. Anthropic is not a safe AI company, and we must reject its reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good." A representative for Anthropic declined to comment about the statement. — Ashley Capoot 1 Hour Ago Anthropic’s explosive revenue growth The Anthropic Claude logo on a smartphone and laptop arranged in San Francisco, California, Nov. 10, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic's revenue has surged dramatically this year as more companies have adopted its AI models and products. The company said it generated roughly $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic's losses also widened, however. It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, compared to a net loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025. The vast majority of its loss, about $94.3 billion, comes from a change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, Anthropic said. The company said its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion as of the end of October, up roughly $10 billion from the previous month. — Ashley Capoot 1 Hour Ago Anthropic’s seven co-founders have majority voting power Anthropic said in its prospectus that it believes its seven co-founders are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission." The co-founders are the sole members of " Founder LLC ," a new entity that holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. The structure gives them "the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future," according to the filing. The co-founders' combined voting power from their holdings and their interest in Founder LLC is expected to be 61.3%, according to the filing. Novartis projected annual sales growth of 5% through 2031, slightly less ambitious than its previous guidance of between 5% and 6% through 2030, although it covers a different five-year period. CEO Vas Narasimhan said the revised outlook reflected the expected entry of U.S. generic competition for Kisqali, a breast cancer treatment, in the second half of 2031. Citi analysts noted the 2031 sales guidance was about 3% above consensus, adding they expect the market to remain skeptical of post-2031 growth, pending further pipeline data. Cholesterol drug setback casts doubt over multibillion-dollar race Novartis has faced several recent clinical setbacks. In September, its closely watched cardiovascular pelacarsen trial failed to show improved cardiovascular outcomes. The following day, its del-desiran drug for muscle-wasting disorder failed in a late-stage trial , sending shares down nearly 11% in its worst single-day drop since 1987. Narasimhan defended the drugmaker's capital allocation strategy after the failure of its experimental drug del-desiran, which it acquired via a $12 billion deal for Avidity Biosciences earlier this year. Shareholders have differing views on acquisitions, with some favouring more aggressive dealmaking and others preferring a different approach, Narasimhan said. However, he said Novartis remained confident in its strategy, pointing to a 275% total shareholder return over the past decade, which he said placed the company among the sector's top performers.
